AdminAgentRemovalImpact.description:
Owner-only impact preview returned before an Agent Removal. It reuses the
same Server-side measurement the mutation performs, so a confirmation
cannot describe a different scope than the one erased.

can_remove.description: False while an unhandled Transfer blocks the removal.

AdminAgentRemovalNode.description:
One Node an Agent authoritatively owns, listed in the removal confirmation
so the Owner sees exactly which Nodes will be permanently purged.

AdminAgentRemovalTarget.description: The exact Agent an Owner is about to remove.

AdminAgentRemovalTransfer.description:
A still-pending Transfer involving the Agent that blocks its removal until
it is completed, cancelled, or expired.

AdminAgentStorageMountsResponse.description:
The mount paths one Agent reported, and the coverage of the storage series
behind each of them (issue #216, design §11.6).

The mount path is the identity of a Host storage series: it is stored as the
series' dimension and compared literally. Without this list an operator has to
guess the exact string, and a path the Agent stopped reporting becomes
unreachable exactly when it matters. The list comes from the stored evidence,
never from a device identifier: same path under a new device is
indistinguishable by contract, and no such identity is invented here.

answeredAt.description: The instant this answer was assembled from.

cadenceSeconds.description:
The rhythm the Agent is observing its Host at now, measured from the
newest stored observations of the Host series that stands for the whole
Host observation, and 0 when that evidence does not show one yet: an Agent
that has just changed its collection interval states no cadence until its
newest interval agrees with the one before it.

capacityMetric.description: The series the `capacity` side of every mount answers with.

collectionPaused.description:
True while low-space protection has optional history paused (design
§11.4). The Agent is still reporting and the Server is choosing not to
store the readings, so no path is answered as silent: what was already
stored stays, and the age of it is not the Agent going quiet.

mountLimit.description:
The number of mount paths this answer can carry, and the bound it keeps:
each storage side is read with this bound, the two are merged by the path
from one snapshot of the ledger, and the merged list is cut at the same
bound in the same order.

mounts.description: The mount paths, most recently observed first, ties settled by the path.

silenceThresholdSeconds.description:
The silence that means "this path is no longer being reported": three
cadences of the Agent's measured cadence, with the cadence a silence is
judged against capped at five minutes, and never less than two minutes;
0 when the cadence is unknown. No silence is ever excused by a cadence
nobody could configure, and no silence is declared while the Server itself
is pausing optional history.

truncated.description:
True when the Agent holds more mount paths than this answer carries: the
newest paths are answered and the oldest ones are left out, stated here
rather than dropped silently.

usedMetric.description: The series the `used` side of every mount answers with.

availability.description: `unavailable` when the requested range extends beyond raw retention.

AdminMetricGap.description:
A stretch of the window in which the Server stores no observation.

Reported as a gap with its kind, so no surface has to bridge silence, hold a
constant value across it, or draw it as a zero (design §11.4).

kind.description:
`collection_gap` (nobody observed) or `protection_pause` (the operator
chose to pause collection).

AdminMetricHistoryResponse.description:
Owner-only metric history for one Node series (issues #213 and #214, design
§11.4 and §11.6): the stored observations of the raw window, the aggregate
buckets that answer the stretches beyond it, the silences between them, and
the state of the series behind them.

aggregateSupported.description:
True while the Server serves the 1-minute and 5-minute tiers for the
stretches older than the raw window (issue #214).

availability.description:
`None` while the whole requested range is answerable, `partial` when it
was clamped to the investigation horizon, `unavailable` when it is older
than any retained history.

continuation.description:
When the answer is truncated, the coordinate to pass back as `before` for
the next, older page. `None` when the answer reaches the oldest end of
the requested range.

dimension.description:
The series' dimension: the mount path of a Host storage series, empty for
every series that exists once per owner.

from.description: The answered range, after clamping to the investigation horizon.

grain.description:
The finest grain this answer carries: `raw`, `1m`, `5m`, or `none`
when no tier holds anything for the requested range.

historyHorizonDays.description:
The oldest age any tier answers, in days: the investigation horizon the
5-minute tier and its retention family both declare.

nodeId.description:
The Node whose page asked for the answer, when a Node page asked. Null on
the Agent route; on a Host answer it names the Node that asked, so no
surface presents shared evidence as one Node's own.

rawRetentionDays.description: The configured raw window, which decides where the raw tier ends.

requestedFrom.description:
The range the caller asked for, so a clamped or paged answer says what it
clamped or narrowed.

scopeKey.description: The identity the series is stored under: the Node ID, or the Agent ID.

scopeKind.description:
`node` when the series belongs to one Node's own process, `host` when it
is the Host series the Agent collected once for every Node on it.

segments.description: Which tier answered which stretch, oldest stretch first.

to.description:
The answered range's end: the requested `to`, or the exclusive paging
cursor when the caller paged with `before`.

truncated.description:
True when any tier had more evidence than the caller's limit: the newest
points are returned and the rest is reported, never dropped silently.

AdminMetricSample.description: One stored raw observation with the timing evidence that belongs to it.

clockSuspect.description: The observation is stamped after the receipt: the Agent clock is ahead.

delaySeconds.description:
`received_at - last_observed_at` for this very point, so spool and
transport delay are visible per observation. Unknown when either
timestamp is unusable — never reported as zero.

firstObservedAt.description:
The oldest observation this point holds: the other end of the stretch it
really testifies to, and equal to `observedAt` for a raw sample. A bucket
whose two ends are far apart states a span, not continuity - a surface
that says how long the point covers must measure it between these two
instants, never from the bucket's own aligned start (review F1).

grain.description: The grain this point was served at: `raw`, `1m` or `5m`.

lastObservedAt.description:
The newest observation this point holds. Equal to `observedAt` for a raw
sample; for a bucket it is the instant inside the bucket that delay and
clock suspicion are measured from.

maxGapSeconds.description:
The widest interval the bucket recorded between two of its consecutive
observations (0 for a raw sample, and for a bucket that counted one).
This is measured evidence about the inside of a bucket: a surface can
compare it with the cadence it sees and draw a line break where the
Server proved a hole instead of a continuous stretch. Zero means the
observations it counted were contiguous, never that nobody measured.

minValue.description:
The extremes of the observations behind this point. A raw sample is its
own extreme; a bucket keeps the spike the raw samples would have shown.

observedAt.description:
The point's coordinate: the observation instant of a raw sample, or the
aligned start of an aggregate bucket.

receivedAt.description:
For a raw sample, the receipt that carried it. For a bucket, the receipt
of the bucket's newest observation.

sampleCount.description:
Observations behind this point: 1 for a raw sample, the bucket's counted
observations for a bucket. A thin bucket says so here instead of looking
like a closed stretch.

source.description:
`raw` for a stored observation, `aggregate` for a bucket that
summarizes observations the raw window no longer holds.

value.description: A raw sample's value, or a bucket's newest value.

AdminMetricSegment.description:
One tier's stretch of a metric-history answer.

It tells the caller which grain answered which stretch, so no surface has to
infer the resolution from the points themselves or present a bucket as if it
were a sample (design §11.6).

from.description:
The stretch this segment answers: the older end inclusive, the newer end
exclusive, matching what the reader asked of the tier.

pointCount.description: Points this answer carries for the segment.

truncated.description:
True when the segment hit the answer's limit, so the stretch holds more
evidence than this answer carries for it.

AdminMetricSeries.description: What the Server knows about the series itself, independent of the window.

correctedCount.description: Observations whose value changed: counted separately too.

coverageSeconds.description: Seconds the samples prove they were observed.

firstObservedAt.description:
The oldest observation ever recorded. It outlives the samples and is not
evidence that raw history survives that far back, and it is deliberately
not called the moment the series was enabled: the Node may have been
collecting before the first Report this Server accepted, so the Server
reports what it has evidence for.

lastObservedAt.description:
The newest observation instant the series ever recorded. A series-level
stamp: it outlives the samples, and it is not evidence that a stored
sample exists at that instant any more.

lastReceivedAt.description:
The receipt time of the delivery that recorded the newest observation:
a series-level delivery stamp, so it can belong to a later restatement of
that instant rather than to the sample the answer carries. The per-sample
receipt is `items[].receivedAt`.

latestClockSuspect.description:
That same newest stored sample is stamped after its receipt: the Agent
clock is ahead of the Server's.

latestDelaySeconds.description:
`receivedAt - observedAt` of the newest stored sample in this answer,
measured from that one row. Unknown when the answer holds no stored
sample — never reported as zero.

observed.description:
False when this Node never reported the series: shown as absent, not as
zero.

replayedCount.description:
Deliveries that restated an observation already stored: counted
separately, never as new observations.

mismatched_node_count.description: Active Nodes whose observed identity contradicts this Registry tuple.

AdminNetworkNode.description:
One Node inside a Network detail: per-Node identity disposition against
the Registry tuple, plus the Server-owned health and lifecycle state.

AdminNodeDetail.description:
Owner-only Node detail: the full per-Node view with Server-owned
metadata, lifecycle guidance, identity disposition, and the independent
process/RPC/sync/consensus observation dimensions (design §4.1–§4.3).

oneOf.description:
Most recent two-phase Transfer for this Node (any outcome), with the
Server-owned effective status; `None` when no Transfer ever existed.

Automatic Validator identity coverage for this Node (#218): the
discovery state, its sanitized reason, and the currently open automatic
Link interval. `None` only when the Node row disappeared between the
metadata read and this projection; `not_evaluated` means the discovery
dimension has never examined the Node.

AdminNodeListItem.description:
Owner-only Node inventory row: Server-owned metadata (display name,
visibility, lifecycle guidance) stays distinct from Agent-observed
identity and endpoint configuration, and each Node is its own row so
block, transaction, consensus, peer, and error state never merge across
Nodes.

health.description: Server-owned Node Health Summary severity and primary reason.

updated_at.description: Last Server-side metadata change (display name / visibility).

AdminNodePurgeCounts.description:
Server-computed scope of a Node Purge. These are counts of Node-owned rows
only; shared Agent/Host/Network/Validator data is never included.

AdminNodePurgeImpact.description:
Owner-only impact preview returned before a Purge. It reuses the same
Server-side measurement the mutation performs, so a confirmation cannot
describe a different scope than the one deleted.

AdminNodePurgeTarget.description:
The exact Node an Owner is about to delete, with Server-owned metadata and
the latest Inventory lifecycle. It is deliberately separate from the
purge counts so the confirmation shows identity and impact distinctly.

AdminNodeValidatorIdentity.description:
One Node's automatic Validator identity coverage on the Owner-only Admin
surface (#218, main design §15.4). Every field is Server-owned evidence: the
discovery state, the sanitized reason, and the currently open automatic Link
interval. Nothing here is a manual role, an ownership claim, or a
consensus-membership statement.

associationEffective.description:
Whether the Public projection also shows this association: Public
requires an Active Node, so an inactive Node keeps its identity history
without a projected correspondence.

evaluatedAt.description: When the discovery dimension last evaluated this Node.

observedValidatorNodeKey.description: The full P2P public key currently observed from this Node.

reason.description: Sanitized explanation carried by every state except `identified`.

state.description:
Discovery state of the last evaluation, or `not_evaluated` when the
discovery dimension has never examined this Node.

validatorId.description: The Validator of the currently open automatic Link interval, if any.

validatorNodeKey.description: That Validator's own chain identity key.

attention.description:
Server-owned attention queue. The WebUI presents these items and
never recomputes health policy or attention in the browser.

five_minute.description:
The fixed newest tail of five-minute buckets, answered when no range was
asked for.

hourly.description:
The fixed newest tail of hourly buckets, answered when no range was asked
for.

oneOf.description:
The bounded range this answer covers, when one was asked for: a ranged
read fills this and leaves both tails empty, so one response never means
two things.

state.description:
Aggregate collection state; retained last-good rows remain visible
when the latest Peer collection is in error.

AdminPeerRange.description:
One bounded read of a Node's Peer receipt buckets (issue #220).

Receipt buckets are what the Server actually accepted, so a range says how
many of them it holds, where the grain's own grid expects more of them, and
which older page comes next. A fixed top list silently leaves everything
older than its limit unreadable, and a window that cannot be paged cannot
rule that out.

continuation.description:
Pass this as `before` for the next, older page while `truncated`: a
bucket start is unique inside a Node and grain, so paging at a tie cannot
skip or repeat a bucket.

coverage.description:
`complete`, `partial`, `empty` or `unavailable`, the vocabulary the
investigation window uses.

first_bucket.description: The oldest and newest bucket the range holds, when it holds any.

from.description:
Start of the answered range: a bucket belongs to it when its start is at
or after `from` and before `to`.

matching.description: How many buckets the range holds in total, whatever the page limit is.

missing_buckets.description:
Aligned buckets the Node's own stretch expects inside the range and the
Server holds none for: a receipt bucket exists only when a Report carried
Peer evidence, so each of them is a receipt that never arrived. The grid
starts at the oldest bucket the grain ever recorded, so the era before a
Node's first successful snapshot is never counted here.

truncated.description: True when the range holds more buckets than the page limit returned.

AdminStateEntry.description:
One recorded state of a Node component, with the timing evidence that
belongs to it.

The evidence of a state is a state vector, never a number: the collection
state, where the value came from, which failure was reported and the sync
flag as it was observed. A failure is therefore recorded as a failure, and a
value the Agent could not refresh keeps the instant it was really observed
at, so no surface has to invent a transition or read Unknown as zero
(design §11.7, §5.1; issue #217).

clockSuspect.description: The observation is stamped after the receipt: the Agent clock is ahead.

delaySeconds.description: The Agent-to-Server delay of this delivery.

entryKind.description:
`change` for a delivery whose state differs from the state before it,
`anchor` for one that re-recorded an unchanged state.

errorCode.description: The failure the Agent reported, when the collection failed.

observedAt.description: The instant the Node was heard from: the entry coordinate.

receivedAt.description: The instant the Server received the Report that carried it.

syncing.description:
The sync flag, present only where the collection succeeded: a failed
probe is unknown, never false.

valueObservedAt.description:
The instant of the value this state refers to. It is older than
observed_at for a last-good state, so the age of the value can be read
instead of a fresh-looking timestamp.

AdminStateGap.description:
A stretch of the window in which the record shows nothing, because either
nobody reported or protection paused recording.

Reported as a gap with its kind, so no surface bridges silence with a
constant state, calls a missing report a normal period, or reads a pause as
a change (design §11.7, §11.5; issue #217).

kind.description:
`collection_gap` (nobody observed) or `protection_pause` (the operator
chose to pause collection).

AdminStateHistoryResponse.description:
Owner-only recorded state history for one Node component (issue #217,
design §11.7): the recorded state changes and hourly anchors, the
silences between them, and the state of the series behind them.

anchorSeconds.description:
How long an unchanged state may go unrecorded before an anchor is
written, so a reader can tell an unchanged state from a missing report.

availability.description:
`None` while the whole requested range is answerable, `partial` when it
was clamped to the retention horizon, `unavailable` when it is older than
any retained history.

cadenceSeconds.description:
The reporting cadence of the Node, or zero when it is unknown: the
cadence the silences were judged against.

continuation.description:
When the answer is truncated, the coordinate to pass back as `before` for
the next, older page.

from.description: The answered range, after clamping to the retention horizon.

requestedFrom.description:
The range the caller asked for, so a clamped or paged answer says what it
clamped or narrowed.

retentionDays.description:
The configured window of this family, which is also its whole horizon:
recorded states have no aggregate tiers.

to.description:
The answered range end: the requested `to`, or the exclusive paging
cursor when the caller paged with `before`.

truncated.description:
True when the window held more entries than the caller limit: the newest
are returned and the rest is reported, never dropped silently.

AdminStateSeries.description:
What the Server knows about the recorded-state series itself, independent of
the requested window.

anchorCount.description: Counted deliveries that re-recorded an unchanged state.

changeCount.description: Counted deliveries that recorded a state change.

correctedCount.description: Deliveries that disagreed with the row already held for their instant.

coverageSeconds.description:
The seconds the returned entries account for: only the stretch between
two recorded states counts, never the stretch after the newest one.

entriesReturned.description: How many entries this answer carries.

entryCount.description:
Counted deliveries, including the ones that wrote no row because the
state had not changed.

firstObservedAt.description:
The oldest instant the series ever counted, even when its row was
released.

lastObservedAt.description: The newest instant the series ever counted.

lastReceivedAt.description: The instant the newest counted Report arrived.

latestCollectionState.description:
The state of the newest counted delivery, which is the Server latest
word on this component even when its row was released.

observed.description:
False when this Node never had a state recorded: shown as absent, not as
a state.

releasedBefore.description:
The floor this series last stamped for evidence its window released, so
a missing early entry is a boundary and not a quiet start.

replayedCount.description: Deliveries of an instant the log had already counted.

AdminStorageMount.description: One mount path the Agent reported, with both storage series behind it.

mountPath.description:
The path exactly as the Agent reported it. It is the whole identity of
the series: the Server compares it literally and never normalizes it, so
two spellings of one filesystem are two series, and two filesystems that
swap places behind one path are not claimed to be distinguishable.

observationState.description:
`reported` while the Agent is still observing this path at its measured
cadence, `silent` when it has said nothing for longer than that cadence
allows, `unknown` when the Agent's cadence cannot be measured from the
stored evidence. A slow cadence is never mistaken for silence.

silentSeconds.description:
Seconds since the newest observation of this path, null when the Server
has no cadence to judge a silence against or is holding the readings back
itself. An age with no measured cadence is an age, not a verdict.

used.description: Bytes in use on this path (`disk_used_bytes`).

AdminStorageSeries.description:
One storage series of one mount path, in the shape the Agent page reads
(issue #216, design §11.6).

The counts and the boundary come from the series' ledger, which outlives the
samples: the evidence an operator investigates with is the range reader's, and
this answer only says which series hold evidence and how much of it. A series
that was never observed is stated as such rather than as an empty series, and a
series whose readings have been released says so through `releasedBefore`
instead of presenting its boundary as an empty stretch.

firstObservedAt.description: The oldest instant ever observed for this series.

lastObservedAt.description:
The newest instant the Server stores for this series. It stays set after
the readings themselves are released, because the ledger keeps the fact.

latestClockSuspect.description: The newest reading is stamped after its receipt: the Agent clock is ahead.

latestDelaySeconds.description:
`latestReceivedAt - latestObservedAt` for the newest reading, null when
either timestamp is unusable.

latestValue.description:
The newest stored reading, null when the raw window no longer holds one.
Unknown is never reported as zero.

observed.description: True when this mount path was observed for this metric at all.

releasedBefore.description:
The instant before which this series' readings were released by retention,
null while none has been. It is how a missing newest reading is explained:
released on purpose, never "no data was ever collected".

role.description: Legacy manual role; automatic Links carry none (#173).

activity.description:
Canonical last-good Validator Activity (#173): Observing stands for an
authoritative absence as well as for evidence that cannot be observed.

currentValidatorStatusQualifier.description:
`locked` or `exiting` while the staking identity is confirmed valid but
is not normally participating.

currentValidatorStatusState.description:
Currency of the Current Validator Status verdict: `current`, `stale`,
or `unknown`.

lastGoodAgeSeconds.description:
Server-computed age of the last-good observation in whole seconds;
never 0 for a Validator that has never refreshed successfully.

AdminValidatorTrendAssociation.description: One Node association of this Validator that still resolves to a Node row.

current.description: This interval has no end boundary yet.

origin.description: manual or automatic, the model this interval was created under.

AdminValidatorTrendGap.description:
A stretch of configured local days this answer proves holds no snapshot.
A surface draws it as silence, never as a zero.

AdminValidatorTrendMonth.description:
One configured calendar month the answer touches, with the month boundary
mapped into the UTC investigation coordinate (#219).

monthEnd.description: UTC instant the next month's first configured local day starts at.

monthStart.description: UTC instant the month's first configured local day starts at.

AdminValidatorTrendPoint.description:
One stored configured calendar day of the trend, with the UTC instants that
local day really covers and the timestamps the bucket was chosen from.

clockSuspect.description:
The observation is stamped after its receipt: the Provider clock is
ahead of the Server clock.

dayEnd.description:
UTC instant the next configured local day starts at, exclusive. A
daylight-saving day is 23 or 25 hours wide here instead of a pretended 24.

dayStart.description: UTC instant the configured local day starts at, inclusive.

delaySeconds.description:
receivedAt minus providerTimestamp in whole seconds for this one row.
Null when the observation carried no Provider timestamp, because then
there is no delay to measure; never 0 for an unknown delay.

sampleTime.description:
Which timestamp chose this calendar day: the Provider timestamp or the
Server receipt time.

answeredFromLocalDate.description: The configured local dates this answer really covers.

associationHistoryPartial.description:
True when deleted Nodes mean this association list is not the whole
association history. Retained Validator snapshots are never dropped.

associations.description: Association intervals that still resolve to a Node row.

clamped.description: The requested window was narrowed to the bounded maximum window.

continuation.description: Pass this back as before for the next, strictly older page.

counterSemantics.description:
The counters in this answer are cumulative Provider counters as of each
sample. This endpoint never derives period earnings, net profit, or a
silently UTC re-bucketed series from them.

coverage.description:
The coverage verdict this answer carries on its own: complete, partial,
unavailable (nothing observed in the stretch), or empty (the caller
asked for a stretch of no days).

deletedNodes.description:
Nodes of this Validator's Network that Purge already deleted. Purge
removes that Node's association rows with the Node, so those intervals
are unavailable here rather than never having existed (Story 68).

expectedDays.description:
Days the answered stretch covers, days that carry a snapshot, and the
difference, so coverage is disclosed instead of assumed.

foreignRows.description:
Stored rows for this Validator inside the answered stretch that were
formed in another timezone. They are disclosed here and never merged
into the configured calendar.

points.description: Points in ascending configured local-date order.

requestedFrom.description:
The UTC coordinate the caller asked for, echoed so a clamped or paged
answer says what it narrowed.

timezone.description:
The configured IANA timezone every local date in this answer is formed
in. A stored bucket from another zone is counted, never merged.

truncated.description: The window holds more days than the caller's limit answered.

AgentAttentionAcknowledgmentRequest.description:
One Owner acknowledgment request: the exact Agent Attention Items and
evidence boundaries the Owner saw, never a bare kind or a "hide forever"
switch (design §15.6, webui.md §15.3).

acknowledged.description: Boundaries applied to the current occurrence.

attention.description:
Authoritative unacknowledged Agent Attention Items *after* the
mutation; the WebUI refetches rather than hiding the row locally.

skipped.description: Boundaries skipped because newer evidence superseded them.

AgentAuditItem.description:
One redacted Audit row for an Agent lifecycle event. The stored
`after_json` bodies are redacted by construction: they carry ids,
instants, and counts, never token or credential plaintext.

AgentCredentialSummary.description:
Redacted Agent credential summary. Only the non-sensitive credential
id and lifecycle instants are exposed; the credential secret itself is
never stored by the Server and never appears in any Admin DTO.

active.description: Server-computed validity: not revoked and not past `revoke_after`.

revoke_after.description:
Rotation overlap deadline; the credential stops authenticating at
this instant even without an explicit revoke.

attention.description:
Server-owned, currently unacknowledged Agent Attention Items with
their occurrence/evidence boundaries (issue #172). The Agent Detail
page renders these instead of rebuilding warning predicates from
cumulative counters, so an acknowledged occurrence stays suppressed
while raw evidence remains in Diagnostics.

credentials.description:
Credential state as a separate dimension (design: identity,
liveness, boot/report, inventory, credentials, diagnostics).

display_name.description:
Owner-editable Server-owned display name (design §15.2). `None` means
the WebUI identifies the Agent by its stable ID.

inventory.description:
Server-owned Inventory diagnosis (issue #181): the revision/hash the
Server currently accepts, and the Agent's latest Inventory-caused
rejection. Node `inventory_revision` is the per-Node accepted revision;
this is the Agent-wide Inventory declaration.

AgentInventoryDiagnostic.description:
What the Server currently accepts for one Agent's Node Inventory, and which
declaration it refused last (issue #181). The pair is what makes the remedy
obvious: the Agent declares revision `reported_revision` with hash
`reported_sha256`, while the Server accepts `accepted_revision` with
`accepted_sha256`.

The declaration protocol is Server-recorded (issue #188). A v2
(Server-managed) declaration carries no Agent-assigned revision, so it is
explained from the Server-assigned revision/canonical fingerprint plus the
actual refusal evidence, never from a fabricated Agent revision. An Agent
whose declaration was never accepted has no accepted revision at all, which
is distinct from an accepted empty Inventory.

accepted_declaration.description:
Which protocol produced the accepted declaration: `server_managed`
(v2), `agent_declared` (v1), or `unknown` when nothing has been
accepted or the evidence predates this field.

accepted_revision.description:
The revision of the currently accepted Node Inventory: Server-assigned
for a v2 declaration, Agent-declared for v1. `None` means the Server has
never accepted a declaration from this Agent.

accepted_sha256.description:
Content hash (v1) or canonical declaration fingerprint (v2) of that
accepted Inventory. `None` means no declaration was ever accepted.

oneOf.description:
The refusal that stopped the Agent's most recent report, when that
report was refused because of its Inventory. `None` means the latest
ingestion attempt was not an Inventory rejection.

AgentInventoryRejectionEvidence.description:
Server-recorded evidence of one whole-report Inventory rejection. All of it
is Server-computed or Server-stored; nothing here is Agent-reported
diagnostics.

declaration.description:
Which protocol produced the refused declaration: `server_managed` (v2)
or `agent_declared` (v1). A v2 refusal declares no revision.

received_at.description: When the Server stored the refusing Report Receipt.

reported_revision.description:
The Inventory revision the refused report declared. `None` for a v2
(Server-managed) declaration, which declares no revision.

reported_sha256.description:
The Inventory content hash (v1) or canonical declaration fingerprint
(v2) the refused report declared.

displayName.description:
Server-owned display name. Absent, `null`, or an empty value clears
the name; the stable Agent ID remains the identifier (design §15.2).

notes.description: Free-form Owner notes. Absent, `null`, or an empty value clears them.

AgentRemovalPurgedNode.description: One Node permanently purged by the Agent Removal.

AgentRemovalRequest.description:
Owner-confirmed Agent Removal request. The echoed Agent ID and the Node ID
list are a scope re-check, never the authorization boundary: the Server
still re-measures ownership inside the mutation transaction and refuses to
delete a Node the Owner did not confirm.

AgentRemovalResponse.description:
Authoritative completion of an Agent Removal. The response is only produced
after the transaction that revoked the credentials, purged the owned Nodes,
marked the Agent removed, and appended the Audit Event has committed.

expectedVersion.description:
Version of the Rule that this edit was composed against. The save is
rejected when it no longer matches the stored version (issue #204,
Story 19): a stale tab can never silently overwrite a newer edit.

ApiErrorBody.description:
Unified API error envelope (design §13.3): clients depend only on `code`;
`message` never leaks SQL, RPC URLs, credentials, or stacks; `requestId`
correlates a response with its request log; `fields` carries per-field
validation details when a later ticket adds them.

AttemptRow.description: One recorded provider attempt (redacted provider result).

AttentionAcknowledgment.description:
One Item reference the Owner echoed back. The boundary is opaque to the
browser; the Server only needs to match it against the current evidence.

evidence_key.description:
Server-owned occurrence/evidence boundary. An Owner acknowledgment
echoes this value back and applies only while it is still current, so
new evidence is never swallowed by a stale confirmation. The WebUI
treats it as opaque.

id.description: Stable item key (kind + subject) for list rendering and tests.

observed_at.description:
Last authoritative observation time for this item. None means the
Server has no observation timestamp for the evidence; it is never
replaced with the snapshot generation time, which is not an event or
observation time.

AttentionKind.description:
The Server-owned Agent Attention kinds (design §8.4.2). Node, Network, and
Settings kinds are never acknowledgeable.

AuditItem.description:
One immutable, redacted Audit row. `details` is the stored `after_json`
body, which is redacted by construction (ids, instants, and counts only
— never passwords, tokens, credentials, endpoints, raw peer IPs, or
complete request bodies).

nextBefore.description: Cursor for the next older page; absent when the listing is complete.

verifyOperationId.description:
The most recent Operation that verified this artifact, so the page can
link the recorded outcome to the task that produced it. Absent means no
verification task ever recorded a result for this artifact.

CapacityIntervalDto.description:
One protection interval: why it opened, what was skipped, and, once the
filesystem recovered, the measurement that closed it.

endedAt.description: Null while protection is still active.

skippedSampleCount.description:
Optional readings counted as skipped during this interval, every series
together. Recorded synchronization and consensus states are optional
readings too, so they are counted here beside the metric samples.

skippedSeries.description: The series that skipped the most readings, bounded.

skippedSeriesTotal.description: How many series counted at least one skipped reading.

CapacityOverview.description: Capacity visibility and low-space protection state for Operations.

mountPath.description: The directory that is measured, null when it cannot be resolved.

pauseBelowBytes.description: Null when the policy is disabled, because nothing is invented in its place.

policyOrigin.description: The configuration file the policy was read from.

oneOf.description:
The newest successful measurement. It is retained as the last good one
when a later sampling attempt fails, so it explains the current
protection decision rather than proving the filesystem is measurable.

sampledAt.description: When the newest successful measurement was taken.

samplingError.description:
Set when the most recent sampling attempt failed, while the last good
measurement above is retained.

transitionError.description: Set when a protection transition could not be recorded durably.

CapacitySampleDto.description: One measurement of the filesystem that holds the Server state.

availableBytes.description: The bytes still available to the Server user.

CapacitySkippedSeriesDto.description: One series whose optional history lost readings while protection was active.

dimension.description:
The series' dimension: the mount path of a Host storage series, empty for
every series an owner and metric identify on their own. Two mounts of one
Host are two series, so their losses are counted apart rather than merged.

firstSkippedAt.description: The first skipped observation, in RFC 3339.

lastSkippedAt.description: The most recent skipped observation, in RFC 3339.

metric.description: The optional metric that was skipped.

scopeKey.description: The node or agent identity the series belongs to.

skippedCount.description:
How many readings this series counted as skipped. Counting follows the
recorded high-water mark, so an accepted Report retry that re-sends the
newest reading is never a second lost sample and the number never
claims more losses than the series accounted for.

destination.description: Redacted destination summary (last four characters only).

providerRef.description: Redacted provider reference (secret file base name only).

deduplicated.description:
True when the Server reconciled to an existing command result instead
of performing another external send.

requestId.description: The Owner-supplied request id this Server command is keyed by.

deduplicated.description:
True when the Server reconciled to an existing command result instead
of re-arming another external action.

requestId.description: The Owner-supplied request id this Server command is keyed by.

DeliveryRow.description:
One Notification Delivery row (redacted by construction: `destination`
is a masked summary and `last_result` is a fixed provider vocabulary,
never raw provider output).

EffectiveRuleDto.description:
The Rule configuration that currently applies to one subject after
Network/Node override resolution (issue #204, Story 20). This is the
current effective configuration and is deliberately separate from the
Incident's immutable opening rule version and evidence.

EnrollResponse.description:
Success payload of one Agent Enrollment (Agent wire: snake_case,
design §9.1). `credential` is the full `pp_agent_…` token and is
delivered to the enrolling Agent exactly once; the Server stores only
its pepper-keyed digest.

agent_epoch.description: Agent Epoch advanced by this Enrollment (1 for a new Agent).

agent_id.description: Stable Agent identity issued by the Server (UUID).

credential.description: Full Agent Credential token; single delivery.

protocol_version.description: Agent→Server protocol major the Server speaks.

EnrollmentTokenResponse.description:
One-time Enrollment Token issued to an Owner (design §4.5, §12.5). The
full token is delivered exactly once in the success response.

disclosure.description:
The exact consequence of selecting this provider, including its fixed
destination, or null for a provider that keeps addresses on this
Server. The Server owns the sentence because it owns the destination:
the browser renders this string and never composes one, so the
disclosure and the endpoint a request is really sent to cannot drift
apart.

sends_peer_addresses.description:
Whether selecting this provider sends observed Peer public addresses
to a third-party service. The Settings surface reads this Server-owned
flag instead of hardcoding which providers do it, so an Owner always
knows the privacy boundary before selecting.

unavailable_reason.description:
Safe explanation when the option cannot be selected. It never contains
a filesystem path, raw address, or provider internals.

started.description:
False when this request joined the identical run that was already in
progress instead of scheduling a second batch.

GeoRefreshStatus.description:
One Owner-triggered global refresh run (issue #136). Every count is a
count of address lookups. `peer_records_in_scope` keeps the Public
projection's per-Node Peer-record denominator beside them, so the two
units are never conflated.

abort_code.description: A stable machine-readable reason when the run stopped early, or null.

abort_reason.description:
The matching non-sensitive sentence, or null when the run is running
or completed.

completed_lookups.description:
Lookups that reached an authoritative outcome. It stays below
`total_lookups` while the run is running or after it was aborted.

peer_records_in_scope.description:
Current Peer records that reference those addresses. One address may
serve several records, so this is never derived from the lookup count.

rate_limited_lookups.description:
Requests the provider refused while rate limiting this Server. A
rate-limited request is not a result and never counts as completed.

run_id.description: An opaque run identifier. It carries no address.

total_lookups.description:
Distinct public Peer addresses the run resolves. One lookup per
address; this is not a count of Peer records.

cache_country_count.description: Distinct countries with a currently valid retained result.

configured.description: Whether this deployment configured a local GeoLite2 Country database.

pending_lookup_count.description:
Current Peer addresses still waiting for a fresh country result. It is
null while Geo is disabled, because nothing is scheduled then.

provider.description: The selected provider. Only implemented providers are ever reported.

provider_generation.description:
Monotonic configuration generation. Every background result carries
the generation that scheduled it and is discarded if it no longer
matches the selection.

rate_limited_until.description:
The bounded backoff window an external provider currently imposes, or
null when the provider may be asked again now. It is a Server-owned
instant: no address, endpoint, or provider error crosses this DTO.

oneOf.description:
The global refresh run the Settings surface reports: running, or the
terminal result of the newest run, or null when no refresh has been
requested since this Server process started.

refresh_unavailable_reason.description:
Why the global refresh cannot start in this configuration, or null
when it can. It is a stable, path-free sentence, so a Disabled
provider is explained before the Owner clicks anything.

state.description:
Effective database/result state: disabled, current, stale, or error.
It is independent of Peer collection freshness and Node health.

HistoryWindowResponse.description:
The MVP global Block History window. This is backed by the raw Block
Summary retention policy; the dedicated DTO keeps the public Admin seam
aligned with the product contract instead of exposing retention families.

IncidentAcknowledgment.description:
The durable, shared Owner confirmation recorded against one Incident
occurrence (parent #202, issue #203). The identity and time are the
accountable facts: the first successful request is authoritative and later
requests never overwrite them.

IncidentAcknowledgmentResponse.description: The authoritative result of an Owner acknowledgment request.

auditEventId.description: Audit Event id of the first confirmation; absent on a no-op repeat.

recorded.description:
True when this request recorded the acknowledgment; false when an
earlier request had already confirmed the same Incident occurrence.

oneOf.description: Present once an Owner durably confirmed this Incident occurrence.

Current effective Rule configuration for this subject, after
Network/Node override resolution (issue #204, Story 20). None when the
Rule or subject kind cannot be resolved. A disabled current Rule means
the evaluation row, when present, is the last recorded assessment
rather than a current one; this never rewrites the Incident's opening
rule version or evidence.

subjectDeletedAt.description:
Set once the subject (Agent/Node) was permanently deleted (design
§15.7, issue #175).

oneOf.description: Present once an Owner durably confirmed this Incident occurrence.

subjectDeletedAt.description:
Set once the subject (Agent/Node) was permanently deleted. The
Incident keeps its original facts and open/resolved state; the
annotation only records that the subject is gone (design §15.7).

continuation.description:
When the answer is truncated, the coordinate to pass back as `before`
for the next, older page.

coverage.description:
`complete` when this answer holds every Incident the window matches,
`partial` when the limit cut it short, `empty` when the window holds
none. An occurrence is never averaged into a value, so a window with no
Incident is empty and not zero (design §11.4; issue #220).

returned.description: How many Incidents this answer carries.

total.description:
How many Incidents the filters match inside the answered window,
independent of `limit`: a cut page still says what it left out.

truncated.description:
True when the range held more Incidents than the caller limit: the newest
are returned and the rest is reported, never dropped silently.

oneOf.description:
The answered occurrence range, absent when the caller asked for the whole
history instead of a range.

IncidentRangeResponse.description:
The occurrence range an Incident list answered (issue #220).

An Incident belongs to the range when it opened inside it or was still open
when the range started, so the answer holds every occurrence the range could
observe and a caller investigating the range reads the same set the
investigation answer points at.

InvestigationAnswerPathResponse.description: Where the evidence behind a source is answered by the Server.

note.description: How to read the response, when it needs saying.

path.description: The request path, including the window this investigation was resolved over.

InvestigationBoundaryResponse.description: One stretch of the window a source cannot answer, and why.

at.description: The instant the boundary starts at.

detail.description: Why this stretch cannot be answered.

kindLabel.description: The label shown beside the kind.

to.description: The instant the boundary ends at, when it ends inside the window.

InvestigationComponentResponse.description: One collector row the Server holds for the investigated subject.

componentKey.description: The collector's key as the Server stores it.

errorCode.description: The error code the last failed collection carried.

observedAt.description: The instant the Agent attempted the last collection.

receivedAt.description: The instant the Server received the last collection.

scope.description: The scope the collector was recorded in (`node` or `host`).

scopeKey.description: The scope's own key (the Node id, or `host` for the Host scope).

InvestigationGrainResponse.description: What one grain of a source can answer for the window.

available.description:
Whether this grain holds any point inside the window.

A grain that serves the window but stored nothing is not available: an
empty grain and a grain that holds an empty stretch are different
statements, and only the counts distinguish them.

cadenceSeconds.description: The fastest interval the grain actually showed, in seconds.

expectedPoints.description: How many points an unbroken grain would hold, when that is knowable.

firstObservedAt.description: The oldest point of this grain inside its stretch.

from.description: The stretch of the window this grain serves, when it serves any.

grainSeconds.description: The bucket width, when the grain has one.

holes.description: The interruptions this grain proves, longest first (at most one per tier).

lastObservedAt.description: The newest point of this grain inside its stretch.

longestGapSeconds.description: The longest interval between two adjacent points, in seconds.

missingPoints.description: How many expected points are missing, when that is knowable.

note.description: Why the grain is unavailable, or how to read its counts.

pointCount.description: How many stored points of this grain fall inside its stretch.

sampleCount.description: How many observations those points aggregate.

to.description: The stretch of the window this grain serves, when it serves any.

InvestigationHoleResponse.description: One located interruption in a grain's evidence.

from.description: The instant the interruption starts after.

seconds.description: How long the interruption lasted, in seconds.

series.description: The series the interruption was measured on, when the grain holds many.

to.description: The instant the interruption ends at, where evidence resumes.

InvestigationPresetResponse.description: One selectable window, as reported to a client.

hours.description: How far back the preset reaches, in hours.

key.description: The value the `window` query parameter accepts.

InvestigationRelatedSubjectResponse.description:
One subject a source's evidence is attributed to, and the Server record that
attribution rests on.

A source answers about its own subject, but some of its evidence belongs to a
subject the Node is related to (the Agent that reported it, its Host, its
Network, a linked Validator). Each such attribution states which subject it is,
whether that subject is the source's own or a related one, and the recorded
basis (the extent of a recorded relationship or Validator link) it is read
over. Nothing is attributed outside a record: a stretch the Server never
recorded is reported as an unknown boundary instead (stories 60, 61).

basis.description: The machine-readable basis of the attribution.

basisLabel.description: The label shown beside the basis.

detail.description: What the record says, and how far it may be read.

from.description: The instant the recorded basis starts at, clipped to the window.

role.description: Whether this is the source's own subject (`source`) or a related one (`related`).

subject.description: The related subject's own key, as the Server records it.

subjectKind.description: The kind of the related subject (`agent`, `host`, `network`, `validator`).

to.description: The instant the recorded basis ends at, clipped to the window.

InvestigationResponse.description: The investigation coordinate for one Node and one window.

agentId.description: The Agent that reports this Node.

components.description: Every collector row the Server holds for this Node and its Agent.

displayName.description: The Node's display name, when the Owner set one.

notes.description: Disclosures that shape how the whole answer must be read.

sources.description: Every evidence family, in a fixed order, whether or not it holds evidence.

window.description: The window the answer was resolved over.

InvestigationSourceResponse.description: A family of evidence and how much of the window it can answer.

answerPaths.description: The existing endpoints that answer this source's evidence for the window.

boundaries.description: The stretches of the window this source cannot answer.

components.description: The collectors behind this source, with their last recorded state.

coverageLabel.description: The label shown beside the verdict.

errorCode.description: The error code the last failed collection carried, when there was one.

firstObservedAt.description: The oldest evidence the Server still holds for this source.

grains.description: What each grain of this source can answer.

lastObservedAt.description: The newest evidence the Server holds for this source.

lastReceivedAt.description: The newest receipt of that evidence.

notes.description: Disclosures that shape how the numbers above must be read.

relatedSubjects.description:
The subjects this source's evidence is attributed to, each with the recorded
basis it is read over. Empty when the source answers only about itself and no
subject was recorded as related to it.

releasedBefore.description: The cleanup cutoff the newest release of this source's evidence used.

retainedFrom.description: The instant beyond which this source's cleanup cannot answer, when it has one.

retentionDays.description: The retention this source's oldest served grain is declared with, in days.

sourceState.description: The collection state the Server last recorded for this source, when it records one.

subjectKind.description: The kind of subject this source describes.

timeBasis.description: The clock this source's timestamps belong to.

timeBasisLabel.description: The label shown beside the clock.

truncated.description: Whether the answer omits detail the Server holds (for example further holes).

InvestigationWindowResponse.description: The window an investigation answered over.

answeredAt.description: The instant the Server resolved the window at.

clampedToNow.description: Whether `to` was clipped to `answered_at` because the range ended in the future.

custom.description: Whether the caller named the range explicitly rather than a preset.

durationSeconds.description: The width of the answered range, in seconds.

from.description: The start of the range the Server answered over.

horizonDays.description: The widest window an investigation accepts, in days.

preset.description: The preset key the answer used, or `custom`.

rawRetentionDays.description: How long the raw metric tier reaches back, in days.

requestedFrom.description: The range the caller asked for, before any clipping.

requestedTo.description: The range the caller asked for, before any clipping.

supportedPresets.description: Every window a client may ask for, so it never hardcodes the list.

to.description: The end of the range the Server answered over.

NetworkCreateRequest.description:
Owner-only Registry creation with the complete validated identity tuple
(design §7.1). The Registry is never created from observed Agent text:
this explicit Owner mutation is the only Admin insert path.

NetworkUpdateRequest.description:
Owner-only Registry update: display name and/or identity tuple fields.
Every field is optional, but at least one must change; the merged tuple
is validated and the before/after state is audited. Existing Nodes whose
observed identity now contradicts the tuple surface as typed mismatches;
no Node state is rewritten.

freshness.description:
Server-owned freshness dimension: `current`, `stale`, or `unknown`.
The WebUI formats this state; it never derives it from `Date.now()`.

NodeIdentityStatus.description:
Server-computed identity disposition for one Node: `matched` when every
observed identity field equals the Registry tuple, `mismatched` when any
observed field differs (a blocking diagnostic distinct from RPC Error or
Node Offline), and `unknown` when the Node was never observed.

mismatched_fields.description:
Registry fields that the observation contradicts (empty when state
is `matched` or `unknown`).

displayName.description:
Server-owned display name (design §4.2). Required: 1..=128 visible
characters; clearing is a future explicit operation.

NodePurgeRequest.description:
Owner-confirmed Node Purge request. The echoed Node ID is friction and a
scope re-check, never the authorization boundary; the Server still
re-measures the impact inside the mutation transaction.

NodePurgeResponse.description:
Authoritative completion of a Node Purge. The response is only produced
after the transaction that removed the rows, recorded the deletion
identity, and appended the Audit Event has committed.

retired.description:
Nodes in a non-active lifecycle (e.g. retired); not part of the
health buckets because no observation policy applies to them.

NodeTransfer.description:
Owner-authorized two-phase Node Transfer (design §4.4, issue #46). The
typed status is Server-owned: `pending`, `completed`, `cancelled`,
`expired`, `rejected`, `conflict`, or `identity_mismatch`. A `pending`
row past its Server-authoritative `expires_at` is reported as `expired`
and never auto-extends.

NodeTransferCreateRequest.description:
Create a pending Transfer: Owner picks the target Agent, an expiry
(1..=168 hours, default 72), and an optional operator reason that is
recorded in Audit.

NodeTransferMutationResponse.description:
Mutation receipt for a Transfer create/cancel: the authoritative typed
Transfer plus the request and Audit references for the success view.

role.description: Legacy manual role; automatic Links carry none (#173).

NotificationRequestResult.description:
The durable Server result of one Owner test/retry command, looked up by its
opaque request id after an HTTP timeout or lost response. It deliberately
exposes only the Server's own association: the Delivery's provider outcome
is at-least-once, never exactly-once.

ObservedNetworkIdentity.description:
Agent-observed Network identity tuple (design §7.1). Never overwrites the
Registry: it is presented as a typed observation with a match state.

cancellable.description:
`true` while the Operation is queued or running and no cancel
request is recorded yet (cancel is still allowed).

ParamSchema.description:
Editor schema for one condition parameter, sent to the WebUI so the
typed rule form renders per-rule fields (no free-form DSL ever).

state.description:
`unknown` means no successful Peer Snapshot exists; `empty` means a
successful snapshot exists but no retained interval is available;
`error` means the latest collection failed while retained intervals
and the last-good value remain available.

freshness.description: Server-owned freshness of the latest successful Peer value.

peer_count.description:
`None` means no successful Peer Snapshot has ever been observed;
`Some(0)` is an authoritative successful empty snapshot.

closed_at.description: Server-observed departure boundary; `None` means the interval is open.

duration_seconds.description:
Closed interval duration. Open intervals intentionally have no
duration because their end boundary is not known yet.

opened_at.description: Server-observed arrival boundary of this connected interval.

Person.description:
One allowlisted Person row. Passwords, hashes, and credentials never
leave the Server (design §12.1: People review is safe on ordinary
screens).

sessionCount.description: Active (non-revoked) Session count; never session material.

PublicAccessSettings.description:
Non-sensitive Public access projection: the Site Access Mode and durable
authorization generation. This is the only public
route reachable without a Session in both modes: the WebUI needs it to
decide whether an anonymous visitor may render Home or must sign in. It
carries no DTO from any other namespace and no session material.

PublicConsensusInsight.description:
Node-scoped last-good consensus state projected from Agent reports.
`None` value fields mean no successful consensus observation has ever
been accepted; `Some(0)` is an authoritative zero-height observation.
Consensus membership is Agent-observed pool membership only; it never
creates or infers a Validator identity or Block Production evidence.

epoch.description: Current epoch from the last good consensus observation.

freshness.description: Server-owned freshness of the last successful consensus observation.

highestCommitBlock.description: Highest commit block height from the last good consensus observation.

highestLockBlock.description: Highest lock block height from the last good consensus observation.

highestQcBlock.description: Highest QC block height from the last good consensus observation.

receivedAt.description: Server receipt time for the last accepted consensus observation.

staleSince.description: Server-computed boundary at which the last observation became stale.

state.description:
Agent-reported collection state. The WebUI presents this separately
from freshness and value availability.

validator.description:
Whether the current validator pool contains this Node. `None` means
no successful observation exists; it must never be presented as False.

viewNumber.description: Current view number from the last good consensus observation.

count.description:
Peer records in scope attributed to this country. Records are counted
per Node and are never deduplicated by IP or Peer identity.

staleCount.description:
Of `count`, the records whose country result is retained last-good
data past its cache lifetime. They keep their country and are never
re-counted as Unknown.

availablePeerCount.description:
The `known_country_count` + `unknown_country_count` denominator the
Server actually observed: the same per-Node Peer-record total the
aggregate Peer Insight reports whenever that total is available. The
browser never subtracts an independent Peer total to derive Unknown.

knownCountryCount.description:
Peer records in scope with a retained country attribution, including
retained last-good rows reported as `staleCount` per country. Peer
records are counted per Node and are never deduplicated by IP.
`None` when there is no reliable denominator (`unobserved` or
`unavailable` scope), so Unknown is never read as zero.

scope.description:
How complete the Peer-record basis of this projection is: `complete`
(every Active Node in this Network reported a successful Peer
Snapshot), `partial` (some did), `unobserved` (none did), or
`unavailable`
(no country projection exists because Geo is Disabled or its read
failed; `state` keeps those two apart).

state.description:
Server-owned Geo database state. Raw IPs and MMDB paths never cross
the Public projection boundary. This is the database dimension only:
it never claims that Peers are currently online or freshly observed.

unknownCountryCount.description:
Peer records in the same scope with no retained country attribution.
`None` under the same conditions as `known_country_count`.

unknownWithPublicIpCount.description:
Of `unknown_country_count`, the records that do have a usable public
remote IP but no retained country result. Both reasons are computed
here so the browser never derives one by subtraction; they are never
split further than the Server can substantiate.

unknownWithoutRemoteIpCount.description:
Of `unknown_country_count`, the records without a usable public
remote IP.

validatorSummary.description:
Deduplicated, exact current-selection Cumulative Validator totals for
this Network. The browser selects which Network groups to show; it
never adds up duplicate Node projections itself (#159).

latestBlockTransactionCount.description:
Transaction count from this Node's latest persisted Block Summary.
`None` means the Node has not produced a Block Summary yet.

validatorIdentityReason.description:
Sanitized explanation when this Node has no established automatic
correspondence. It never contains a raw diagnostic or a public key.

validatorIdentityState.description:
Server-owned automatic-identity state for this Node (#173):
`identified`, `missing_public_key`, `invalid_public_key`,
`network_identity_missing`, or `network_identity_mismatch`. `None`
means no automatic discovery pass has run yet. It is separate from
Current Validator Status: identity correspondence can be established
while the Provider still cannot confirm current staking validity.

PublicNodeDetail.description:
Public Node Detail response: every `PublicNode` field plus the Node Peer
Country View over exactly this Node's current Peer records. The Node list
keeps `PublicNode`, so a Home or Network response never carries one country
projection per Node.

state.description:
Aggregate collection state; history absence is never presented as a
healthy zero-valued observation.

freshness.description: Server-owned freshness of the last successful Peer Snapshot.

observedAt.description:
The last successful observation time. No peer identity or address is
included in the Public projection.

peerCount.description:
`None` means no successful snapshot has ever been observed; `Some(0)`
is an authoritative successful empty snapshot.

receivedAt.description: Server receipt time for the last accepted Peer snapshot.

staleSince.description: Server-computed boundary at which the last observation became stale.

state.description:
Agent-reported collection state. The WebUI presents this separately
from freshness and value availability.

PublicValidatorBlockTotal.description:
Per-Network cumulative total for one metric, deduplicated by Validator.

The Server owns the eligible set, the deduplication, the exact arithmetic,
and the coverage metadata, so Home never sums duplicate Node projections.
Coverage is tracked for blocks and rewards independently because one metric
can be missing while the other has a value (#159).

expectedCount.description: Distinct eligible Validators this metric should cover.

knownSum.description:
Exact base-10 integer sum over the eligible Validators, serialized as a
string to avoid both i64 overflow and JavaScript number precision loss.
`None` means no eligible Validator reported a value, never a fabricated zero.

staleCount.description:
Contributing Validators whose value is not current (a retained
last-good value after a failed or aged collection).

state.description:
`complete`, `partial`, or `unknown` coverage of `expected_count`.
`partial` is a known-values subtotal, not a complete total.

valuedCount.description:
Eligible Validators contributing a known value, including retained
stale last-good values.

activity.description:
Canonical last-good Validator Activity (`candidate`, `active`,
`producing`, `exiting`, `exited`, `verifying`, `locked`) or
`observing`/`unknown`.
Home never infers this from names, endpoints, consensus membership,
rank data, or Provider data: only an effective explicit Node Validator
Link exposes it on a Public Node (#100).

activityState.description:
`current`, `stale`, or `unknown` currency of the Activity value.
Provider failure with a last-good Activity is always `stale`, even
when the last-good timestamp is still within the freshness window.

blockCount.description:
Cumulative Validator produced blocks over chain history (PlatScan
`blockQty`), not blocks observed by the monitored Node. `None` means
never observed; `Some(0)` is an authoritative zero (#154).

blockRate.description:
Cumulative actual / cumulative scheduled blocks from the same
observation, as a percentage string without the `%` sign (for example
`90.909091`). The Server never mixes a fresh numerator with an older
denominator. It is **not** an exact missed-block rate: whole-round
scheduled duties are counted before they elapse. `None` is either
unknown or not applicable — see `block_rate_state` (#156).

blockRateState.description:
`ok`, `not_applicable`, or `unknown`. `not_applicable` is a known
zero scheduled-block denominator (no production duties), never 0% or
100%; `unknown` means the pair is incomplete. Only `ok` carries a value
in `block_rate` (#156).

currentValidatorStatus.description:
Server-owned Current Validator Status of the automatically identified
chain identity (#173): `validator`, `not_validator`, or `unknown`.
This is currently valid staking identity, not current consensus
selection or Node Health. `not_validator` requires authoritative
evidence (completed exit or a 200 empty identifier); HTTP 404,
transport failures and unsupported coverage stay `unknown`.

currentValidatorStatusQualifier.description:
`locked` or `exiting` while a confirmed-valid identity is not normally
participating; null for an ordinary candidate/active/producing identity
or for any unknown/negative status.

currentValidatorStatusState.description:
`current`, `stale`, or `unknown` currency of the Current Validator
Status. A retained last-good verdict after a failed refresh is `stale`.

delegationRewardPercentage.description:
The currently effective delegation reward distribution percentage
(PlatScan detail `rewardPer`), normalized to percentage points: the
source's already-scaled `20` is 20%, never 0.20% or 2000%. It is
**not** the annualized `reward_rate`, the operator commission, a
pending next-period ratio, or a back-computed net earning. `None`
means unknown; a legitimate `0` and `100` are preserved (#157).

expectedBlockCount.description:
Cumulative scheduled-block denominator from the **same** successful
observation as `block_count` (PlatScan `expectBlockQty`). `None` means
unknown; `Some(0)` is an authoritative "no scheduled duties" value that
must never be presented as a rate (#156).

genBlocksRate.description:
PlatScan's own 24-hour production rate, normalized to a percentage
string without the `%` sign and taken directly from `genBlocksRate`.
The investigated source sums the preceding seven settlement periods
excluding the current one, so it is not a strict rolling 86,400-second
window, and a source-reported `0` can also mean absent evidence or an
upstream error. `None` means unknown, never a synthesized zero (#156).

rank.description:
PlatScan's position within this Network's complete live-staking ALL
cohort (including candidates), adopted verbatim and independent of the
monitored Node set or Home filters. `None` is never zero and never
means unranked by itself: see `rank_state` (#158).

rankCohortSize.description:
Complete live-staking cohort size from the same successful ranking
fetch; `None` when no complete list has been obtained (#158).

rankFreshness.description:
`fresh`, `stale`, or `unknown` currency of the ranking result, tracked
independently from the detail `freshness` (#158).

rankReceivedAt.description:
Server receipt time of the last successful ranking list fetch. It is
distinct from `received_at`, which is the detail fetch time (#158).

rankState.description:
`ranked`, `unranked`, `error`, `not_configured`, `unsupported`, or
`unknown`. Only a complete successful list fetch can establish
`unranked`; a failed, truncated, duplicated, or drifted fetch keeps the
last-good rank and never fabricates an unranked outcome (#158).

rewardAmount.description:
Gross cumulative Validator rewards over chain history, including the
operator and delegator allocations (PlatScan `rewardValue`). It
excludes principal and ordinary transfers and is **not** the operator's
net earnings: the Server never subtracts `totalDeleReward` and never
derives a historical net value from the current distribution ratio.
`None` means unknown, never zero (#155).

PublicValidatorRewardTotal.description:
Exact-decimal counterpart of `PublicValidatorBlockTotal` for gross
cumulative Validator rewards. `known_sum` is a bounded decimal string in
the Network native unit; it never round-trips through binary floating point.

PublicValidatorSummary.description:
Home's current-selection Cumulative Validator summary for one Network.

Membership is the Network's Active Nodes; temporarily offline Active Nodes
stay in scope and Retired Nodes do not. Every distinct Validator referenced
by an effective Node Validator Link is counted once regardless of primary,
standby, or observer role, and Validators are never shared across Networks.
Totals can fall when filters, effective Links, or Active membership change;
they are not an ownership ledger and are not guaranteed monotonic (#159).

eligibleValidatorCount.description: Distinct eligible Validators referenced by an effective Link.

linkedNodeCount.description: Active Nodes with an effective Link.

unlinkedNodeCount.description:
Active Nodes without any effective Link, reported separately so an
unlinked Node is never mistaken for a zero-valued Validator.

RecoverResponse.description:
Success payload of one Recovery exchange (Agent wire: snake_case,
design §4.5). The Agent identity is preserved, the Agent Epoch
advances, and `credential` is a fresh `pp_agent_…` token delivered
exactly once.

agent_epoch.description: Agent Epoch advanced by this Recovery exchange.

agent_id.description: The existing Agent identity the Recovery Token was bound to.

credential.description: Full Agent Credential token; single delivery.

protocol_version.description: Agent→Server protocol major the Server speaks.

RecoveryTokenResponse.description:
One-time Recovery Token issued for an existing Agent. Exchanging it
advances the Agent Epoch and rotates the credential without creating a
duplicate Agent (design §4.5).

RequestIdBody.description:
Mutation body carrying the Owner's opaque request id. The browser
generates it once per Owner intent; the Server uses it for request-level
dedup and stable result lookup.

confirmation.description: Typed confirmation: must equal the artifact file base name.

RestoreValidation.description:
Read-only Restore validation outcome (issue #51, design §20.2): the
Server re-verifies the artifact file against its recorded manifest
before any confirmation. Checksum and integrity are re-computed from
the file; schema compatibility compares the artifact schema with the
current Server schema (higher unsupported schemas are refused). Checks
run in order and short-circuit, so `None` means the check was not
reached (the first failed check is reported in `error`).

checksumOk.description:
`true` when the file checksum matches the manifest; `None` when the
checksum check was not reached.

error.description:
Typed validation failure code when any check fails; `None` when the
artifact is restorable.

integrityOk.description:
`true` when the full integrity check passed; `None` when it was not
reached.

schemaCompatible.description:
`true` when the schema is supported; `None` when it was not
reached.

estimatedRows.description: Rows that would be removed; `None` for unsupported families.

oneOf.description:
The newest preview that still binds, so a reloaded page executes the
same reviewed plan instead of composing a new one.

policyVersion.description:
Fingerprint of this exact policy value. The edit form submits it back so
a concurrent edit can never be overwritten silently.

expectedPolicyVersion.description:
The `policyVersion` the operator read before previewing. Required so a
stale tab cannot overwrite a value it never reviewed.

RetentionPreviewDto.description:
A read-only, expiring impact preview. A run is queued by preview id, so the
estimates the Owner confirmed are the estimates that execute.

estimatedRows.description: Server estimate of the rows the whole preview may release.

scope.description: Absent when the preview covers every actionable policy.

RetentionPreviewFamily.description: One actionable family inside a bound impact preview.

cutoff.description: Rows older than this instant are the only candidates a run may release.

policyVersion.description: Fingerprint of the policy this estimate was composed against.

families.description:
Restrict the preview to these families; absent means every enabled and
supported policy.

RetentionPreviewSkip.description: A requested family the preview will not act on, with the Server's reason.

previewId.description:
The confirmed impact preview. A run never re-estimates impact: the plan
the preview froze is executed as-is, and a preview that expired or no
longer matches the current policies is rejected.

requestId.description:
The Owner's opaque command identity for this confirmation (issue #211).
Re-sending the same id for the same preview reconciles to the recorded
run instead of queueing a second cleanup, and reusing it for a different
command is a conflict.

deduplicated.description:
`true` when the Server reconciled to an already-recorded run for this
requestId or this preview: the Operation below is the recorded one, not
a second run.

requestId.description:
Echo of the command identity the Server keyed this run by, so the
browser can retry the same command and be recognised.

RevokeSessionRequest.description:
Explicit JSON body for Session revoke mutations. The revoke carries no
parameters, but declaring a body keeps the browser trust boundary
uniform: every Admin mutation is a JSON request with the synchronizer
CSRF header (design §12.4), including bodyless ones.

RotationResponse.description:
Rotation result: the new credential secret is shown once; every
previously valid credential either stays valid through `revoke_after`
or was revoked immediately (design §12.6).

RuleCondition.description:
Typed per-rule condition parameters (design §17.1: `for`, recovery
threshold/hysteresis, and an optional typed threshold). `for_secs` is
the sustained firing duration before an Incident opens;
`recovery_for_secs` is the sustained fresh recovery duration before it
resolves. Boolean-fact rules fix their internal threshold at 0.5 and do
not accept a user threshold.

version.description:
Composed configuration revision after this write. Override writes advance
it exactly like a baseline edit, so a second writer still holding the
previous revision is rejected instead of silently overwriting it
(issue #204, Story 19).

expectedVersion.description:
Version of the Rule that this override edit was composed against. The
save is rejected when the Rule has changed since (issue #204).

SessionItem.description:
One coarse, non-sensitive Session row (design §12.3): creation, last
activity, expiry, and a coarse client hint — never the token, a full
User-Agent, or a raw IP.

SessionResponse.description:
Non-sensitive session projection plus the synchronizer CSRF token
(design §12.3/§12.4). Fields are camelCase per the browser wire rule
(§13.3); timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC.

SubjectKind.description: The typed catalog of rule subjects (design §17.1).

SuppressionMatch.description: One active suppression policy matching a subject.

marksIncident.description:
Maintenance-only: whether this match marks the Incident suppressed
(design §17.5). Silences never mark Incidents.

agent_bearer.bearerFormat: Agent Credential (pp_agent_…) or one-time Enrollment Token (pp_enroll_…)
agent_bearer.description: Agent API Bearer token. Enrollment exchanges a one-time pp_enroll_… token for an Agent identity; all other Agent routes require the issued pp_agent_… credential.
